Starlite, a material developed by British hairdresser and amateur inventor Maurice Ward, remains one of science’s most intriguing invention stories. Its reputation grew after a 1990 television demonstration showed a coated egg exposed to a blowtorch, then cracked open to reveal that its contents remained raw. cambridge.org

The striking experiment suggested that a relatively thin protective coating could dramatically limit heat reaching the object underneath. It generated interest in possible applications ranging from fire protection to aerospace equipment. However, a successful demonstration alone does not establish performance across every temperature, exposure duration or industrial environment.

Ward closely guarded the formulation, fearing that others could reproduce his invention. In an interview during his lifetime, he said the recipe had been written down and was known within his immediate family. Commercial negotiations nevertheless failed to turn Starlite into the widely adopted protective material its supporters anticipated.

Ward died in 2011, helping fuel the popular claim that he had taken the formula to his grave. That account is incomplete. American company Thermashield says it acquired Starlite’s technology in 2013, including samples, handwritten formulation notes and other materials from Ward’s family. It also claims to have updated the original formulation. These are the company’s statements, rather than proof of every performance claim associated with Starlite.

Lejos de convertir el mar en un vertedero, los vagones se sumergieron frente a las costas de Delaware, Maryland y Nueva Jersey para crear arrecifes artificiales en fondos arenosos desérticos. Ingredients:
1 package pink frosted sugar cookies
8oz cream cheese (softened)
6 @j@joyconeicecreamcones5313ini ice cream cups
1 cup white chocolate chips
dab of coconut oil
rainbow nonpareils sprinkles

Instructions: 
In a large bowl, mash sugar cookies with room temperature cream cheese and form a dough ball. Separate small sections of cookie dough and form into hollow ice cream cups, flattening the top. Use a muffin tin with dry rice in each opening to stabilize cups while assembling. Additionally, form 6 small balls from remaining cookie dough and allow dough balls to set in the fridge until firm. In a small microwave-safe bowl, microwave white chocolate and coconut oil for 30-second increments, stirring each time until melted with a glossy consistency. Once dough balls are firm, spread a drop of melted chocolate on tops of filled cups and place 1 dough ball on top, using chocolate as "glue" to hold it in place. Allow assembled cups to set in the fridge until firm, then dip in melted white chocolate. Allow all excess to drip off, then cover with rainbow sprinkles and allow cups to set in the fridge until chocolate has hardened. Enjoy! 😋

Yes, we’re dipping the entire burger — and it’s absolutely worth it.

Makes 2 double cheeseburgers

Beef Patties
• 500 g (about 1.1 lb) ground beef
• ½ tsp salt, or to taste
• ½ tsp black pepper
• ½ tsp garlic powder
• ½ tsp onion powder
• 4 cheese slices
• Oil, as needed

Caramelized Onions
• 1 large onion, thinly sliced
• ½ tbsp butter
• ½ tbsp olive oil
• Pinch of salt

Smoky Burger Sauce
• 3 tbsp mayonnaise
• 1 tbsp ketchup
• 1 tsp yellow mustard
• 1 tsp finely chopped dill pickles
• ¼ tsp smoked paprika

Garlic Parmesan Dipping Sauce
• 2 tbsp butter
• 5 garlic cloves, minced
• ¾ cup heavy cream
• ½ cup milk
• ½ cup grated Parmesan
• 1 tsp paprika
• ¼ tsp garlic powder
• ¼ tsp onion powder
• ¼ tsp black pepper
• Salt, to taste
• 1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley

For Assembly
• 2 burger buns
• Butter, for toasting
• Shredded lettuce, optional
• Extra Parmesan + parsley, for garnish

Method

1. Caramelize the onions: Heat butter and olive oil over medium-low heat. Add onion and salt. Cook for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and deeply golden.
2. Make the burger sauce: Mix mayo, ketchup, mustard, pickles and smoked paprika.
3. Cook the patties: Divide beef into 4 portions and loosely shape into balls. Press into thin patties in a hot skillet. Season and cook for 2–3 minutes until browned. Flip, add cheese and cook until the beef reaches 160°F/71°C.
4. Make the garlic Parmesan sauce: Melt butter over medium-low heat and sauté garlic for 30–45 seconds. Add heavy cream and milk, followed by paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper and salt. Simmer gently for 3–5 minutes. Reduce heat and stir in Parmesan until smooth. Finish with parsley.
5. Assemble: Toast the buns with butter. Add smoky burger sauce, 2 cheesy patties, caramelized onions and lettuce. Close and cut each burger in half.
6. Dip & serve: Pour the warm garlic Parmesan sauce into a shallow platter, arrange the burger halves in the sauce and finish with Parmesan and parsley.
